settings.title: Browser dashboard
settings.description: Serve the same live canvas on 127.0.0.1 so you can open it in a browser tab. On by default. Only this computer can reach it, and it needs a secret token.

settings.title: Dashboard port
settings.description: First port to try on 127.0.0.1. The next free one is used if it is busy.

settings.title: Allow controls from the browser dashboard
settings.description: On by default: the browser dashboard can use the same controls as the panel (stop, retry, send messages). Turn off to make it view-only.

settings.title: Act as the Run coordinator
settings.description: On by default. Orca only lets a Run's coordinator create, retry or dispatch tasks; Agent Flow runs those actions with the coordinator's handle after you confirm each one. Turn off to get the exact command to run in the coordinator instead.

settings.title: Orca CLI path
settings.description: Leave empty to find it automatically. Note: on many Linux systems /usr/bin/orca is the GNOME screen reader, which Agent Flow never runs.

settings.title: Send prompts into chat sessions (experimental)
settings.description: Orca's plugin API cannot message chat sessions yet, so Agent Flow uses Orca's own local runtime connection (the one the orca CLI and Orca's mobile app use) for this one action. It may stop working after an Orca update; it then says so instead of sending. Turn off to disable.

settings.title: Check for updates
settings.description: On by default. Every 6 hours Agent Flow asks GitHub (one public request, nothing personal sent) whether a newer version is released, and shows an Update button when there is one. Updating uses Orca's own `orca plugin update`.
